Service area · Chicago and the south suburbs

Where we work, and what is different about each place.

Chicago and the south and southwest suburbs, 27 of them, and they are genuinely not the same job. The city and the inner ring are pre-1978 brick and plaster with heavy trim. The far south and southwest are 1980s and 1990s construction with big elevations and tall interiors. Here is the honest read on each one.

South side and south suburbs, in that order of honesty

The shop is at 7900 W. 83rd St. in Bridgeview, which sits about where the city stops and the southwest suburbs start. That is the whole geography of this business: the south side of Chicago and the towns south and southwest of it. Everything below is built outward from that one address.

Chicago is on this list, and it should not be oversold. The city is a far bigger and far more competitive market than any suburb here, and no small shop covers all of it well. The realistic city work is the south side, Beverly, Mount Greenwood and the neighborhoods around them. Most of the jobs are in the suburbs. If you are on the north side, somebody closer to you will serve you better, and you will get told that on the phone rather than after a missed appointment.

Where the shop is

Bridgeview, IL

  • 4,079 owner-occupied homes
  • 2,146 rented
  • 66% owner-occupied
  • Median value $234,000
  • Median build year 1975

The shop is here, at 7900 W. 83rd St. Nobody in the Bridgeview map pack is actually based in Bridgeview: the three companies holding it are run out of Justice, Burbank and Brookfield. Being ten minutes away is not a marketing line here, it is why a small repair is worth looking at the same week instead of being bundled into next month. Bridgeview housing is split almost evenly between owners and renters, and the median home went up around 1975, so most of it is on its second or third repaint.

Chicago, and the south side in particular

Chicago, IL

  • 522,179 owner-occupied homes
  • 624,368 rented
  • 46% owner-occupied
  • Median value $315,200
  • Median build year 1952

Chicago is the whole city on paper and the south side in practice, and it is worth being straight about which one you are getting. The Bridgeview shop is a short run from Garfield Ridge, Clearing, Ashburn, Beverly and Mount Greenwood, and a long way from the north side. The city is also the oldest housing anywhere in this service area: about 69 percent of Chicago housing units were built before 1970, and roughly four in ten date to 1939 or earlier. In practice that means plaster as well as drywall, painted-shut sash windows, deep millwork, and pre-1978 paint on very nearly everything. Chicago is also a far bigger and far more competitive market than any suburb on this list, so the honest version is south side first, and ask about anything further north before you count on it.

Beverly, Chicago

  • 13,392 owner-occupied homes
  • 4,897 rented
  • 73% owner-occupied
  • Median value $233,900
  • Median build year 1950
  • Figures are for ZIP code 60643, Beverly and Morgan Park

Beverly is bungalow-belt Chicago close to its most intact, with a stretch of larger frame and stucco houses up on the ridge. The 60643 ZIP area, which covers Beverly and Morgan Park, has a median build year of 1950, and about 85 percent of its housing units went up before 1970. On stock that old the paint work is mostly exterior wood and interior trim: sash and storm windows, porch columns, soffit and fascia, and interior casing that is already carrying a lot of coats. It is also as close to a guarantee of pre-1978 paint as anywhere on this list, which changes how an interior job is contained and cleaned rather than how it is painted.

Mount Greenwood, Chicago

  • 9,023 owner-occupied homes
  • 1,794 rented
  • 83% owner-occupied
  • Median value $303,300
  • Median build year 1954
  • Figures are for ZIP code 60655, centered on Mount Greenwood

Mount Greenwood is the most owner-occupied part of the city on this list, about 83 percent, and it is a 1950s neighborhood in a literal sense: four in ten housing units in the 60655 ZIP area were built between 1950 and 1959. That is brick bungalow and Cape Cod stock, smaller rooms, a lot of door and window casing for the square footage, and very often a basement or attic that was finished later and painted to a different standard than the rest of the house. Interior quotes here are decided by trim footage far more than by wall area, which is exactly the line most quotes leave vague.

The near southwest suburbs, roughly fifteen minutes from the shop

Oak Lawn, IL

  • 17,940 owner-occupied homes
  • 3,805 rented
  • 83% owner-occupied
  • Median value $267,900
  • Median build year 1967

Oak Lawn is the biggest suburban market in the close ring by a distance, close to 18,000 owner occupied homes, mostly brick from the mid 1960s. Brick means the paint work is concentrated in the trim, the soffit, the overhead doors and the interior, and it means a lot of interior trim linear footage: heavy casing, six panel doors, full baseboard runs. Trim is where an interior job gets long, and it is the line people forget to ask about.

Burbank, IL

  • 7,761 owner-occupied homes
  • 1,913 rented
  • 80% owner-occupied
  • Median value $258,900
  • Median build year 1965

Burbank has some of the oldest housing in the close ring, a median build year around 1965, and eight in ten households own their home. Almost all of that stock predates 1978, which puts it squarely inside the federal lead-safe renovation rule. That is not a scare line, it is a real difference in how an interior job gets set up, contained and cleaned, and it is worth asking any painter about before they start sanding your window casings.

Evergreen Park, IL

  • 6,109 owner-occupied homes
  • 1,219 rented
  • 83% owner-occupied
  • Median value $255,700
  • Median build year 1955

Evergreen Park has a median build year of about 1955, within a few years of Mount Greenwood and Beverly, and better than eight in ten households own. It behaves like a continuation of the city bungalow belt rather than like a suburb: the same brick, the same trim-heavy interiors, the same pre-1978 answer on every window casing. If you have a bungalow here, the useful question before anybody quotes it is how much of the original trim is still in place, because stripped and replaced casing prices very differently from original casing with sixty years of paint on it.

Palos Hills, IL

  • 5,831 owner-occupied homes
  • 1,496 rented
  • 80% owner-occupied
  • Median value $259,200
  • Median build year 1977

Palos Hills is among the newest housing in the close ring, median build year around 1977, with a large share of townhomes and association-managed buildings. Association work is its own thing: matching an existing scheme exactly, working to a board's schedule and doing several identical units in a row. Worth asking about if you sit on a board.

Palos Heights, IL

  • 4,280 owner-occupied homes
  • 215 rented
  • 95% owner-occupied
  • Median value $350,000
  • Median build year 1976

Palos Heights is among the most owner-occupied places on this list, about 95 percent, with only a couple of hundred renter households in the whole city. There is effectively no turnover or landlord market here. What there is instead is repeat homeowner work on 1970s houses that have generally been kept up: repaints on a cycle, trim and door replacement, and exterior wood that has been maintained rather than left. That is a different job from a neglected exterior and it should be priced as one, in both directions.

Hickory Hills, IL

  • 4,025 owner-occupied homes
  • 1,585 rented
  • 72% owner-occupied
  • Median value $278,400
  • Median build year 1970

Hickory Hills is split levels and raised ranches from around 1970, and that shape of house has a specific problem: a lot of exterior wood in hard places. Soffit, fascia, gable ends and the trim above a split entry all sit high and all fail first. Those are the elevations worth pricing carefully, because the paint on the walls is usually the part that is fine.

Chicago Ridge, IL

  • 2,918 owner-occupied homes
  • 2,391 rented
  • 55% owner-occupied
  • Median value $217,800
  • Median build year 1973

Chicago Ridge runs close to half rental, which makes it two markets in one town. Owners wanting a kitchen or a full interior, and small landlords wanting a unit painted quickly and cleanly between tenants. Both get quoted the same way here: somebody stands in the room first.

Worth, IL

  • 2,835 owner-occupied homes
  • 1,517 rented
  • 65% owner-occupied
  • Median value $220,200
  • Median build year 1967

Worth is 1960s ranch houses on modest lots. On that plan the whole exterior job is usually the garage door surround, the overhang, the front door and the window trim rather than a big wall area, which is a very different quote from a two story with a lot of siding. It is also the kind of job that gets underestimated by anyone quoting off a photo.

Justice, IL

  • 2,475 owner-occupied homes
  • 2,329 rented
  • 52% owner-occupied
  • Median value $235,200
  • Median build year 1976

Justice is one of the most rented places in the close ring: just under half of its households are renters. That means turnover, units that need a full repaint between tenants, on a deadline, priced per unit rather than per room. Not one painting company in this market advertises to landlords or property managers. The van says Maintenance Service on it, which is exactly the right language for this work.

Willow Springs, IL

  • 2,261 owner-occupied homes
  • 350 rented
  • 87% owner-occupied
  • Median value $370,900
  • Median build year 1977

Willow Springs is small, around 2,600 occupied households in total, and unusually high value for its age: a median build year of 1977 but a median home value closer to Orland Park than to its immediate neighbors. A 1977 median also puts roughly half the village on either side of the 1978 lead-safe line, which is a real reason to check the year on your own house rather than assume it from the street.

Summit, IL

  • 2,229 owner-occupied homes
  • 1,388 rented
  • 62% owner-occupied
  • Median value $224,800
  • Median build year 1958

Summit is older than most of what sits immediately around it, a median build year of about 1958, and roughly six in ten households own. Older frame and brick on tight lots usually means the exterior job is scrape, prime and caulk rather than a straight repaint, and an honest quote for that reads longer than one from somebody who has only priced the topcoat. It is also firmly pre-1978 stock, so the lead-safe setup applies as a matter of course.

Bedford Park, IL

  • 161 owner-occupied homes
  • 35 rented
  • 82% owner-occupied
  • Median build year 1947
  • Median value not quoted, residential sample under 200 households

Bedford Park is barely a residential town. The Census counts fewer than 200 occupied households in the entire village, which is why no median home value is shown here: at that sample size the estimate is too thin to be worth quoting, and quoting it anyway is how a website starts stating numbers it cannot stand behind. The few houses that are here have a median build year of 1947. If you manage a building, a unit or a small commercial space here, that work is in scope and it is a very short drive.

The south suburbs

Oak Forest, IL

  • 8,242 owner-occupied homes
  • 2,115 rented
  • 80% owner-occupied
  • Median value $247,800
  • Median build year 1975

Oak Forest is mid 1970s stock and eight in ten households own, which makes it a straightforward homeowner market: whole interiors, full exteriors, kitchens. A 1975 median build year puts a large share of the town just on the older side of the 1978 lead-safe line, so the year on your particular house is worth confirming before an interior job is scheduled rather than after the sanding has started.

Alsip, IL

  • 5,071 owner-occupied homes
  • 2,709 rented
  • 65% owner-occupied
  • Median value $208,700
  • Median build year 1974

Alsip is mid 1970s stock at one of the lower median values on this list, and about a third of its households rent. That mix produces two different calls: owners doing one room or one elevation at a time on a budget, and small landlords wanting a unit turned around between tenants. Both are worth quoting. They are not the same quote, and a contractor who prices them the same way is wrong on one of them.

Midlothian, IL

  • 4,503 owner-occupied homes
  • 1,331 rented
  • 77% owner-occupied
  • Median value $200,300
  • Median build year 1964

Midlothian is mid 1960s stock, largely ranches, with a median value around $200,300 and almost all of it built well before 1978. On a 1960s ranch the exterior work concentrates into a narrow band: fascia, soffit, the garage door surround, the front entry and the window trim. That is not much wall area, but it is all detail and almost all of it is off a ladder, which is exactly why it gets underestimated by anyone quoting from a photo.

Blue Island, IL

  • 4,250 owner-occupied homes
  • 4,412 rented
  • 49% owner-occupied
  • Median value $169,800
  • Median build year 1961

Blue Island and the city of Chicago are the only two entries on this list where renters outnumber owners, and Blue Island has the lowest median home value in the service area at $169,800. Median build year is around 1961. Put those together and the realistic work here is turnover repaints, plaster and drywall repair, and exterior maintenance on older houses, priced tightly and scheduled tightly. It is solidly pre-1978 stock, so lead-safe setup is the default rather than the exception.

Crestwood, IL

  • 3,877 owner-occupied homes
  • 1,143 rented
  • 77% owner-occupied
  • Median value $187,700
  • Median build year 1975

Crestwood is mid 1970s housing at one of the lower median values on this list, around $187,700, with about three quarters of households owning. On budgets in that range the useful conversation is not the total, it is sequencing: what genuinely has to be done this season to stop it costing more later, and what can wait a year at no penalty. A straight answer to that is worth more than a discount.

Further out, south and southwest. Ask about scheduling

Orland Park, IL

  • 20,139 owner-occupied homes
  • 3,214 rented
  • 86% owner-occupied
  • Median value $349,400
  • Median build year 1988

Orland Park is later stock, a median build year around 1988, and bigger houses. Late 1980s and 1990s construction is now hitting its second or third full exterior cycle, and the failure points are different from the older ring: cedar and engineered siding, large two story elevations, and a lot of it. It is further from the shop, so ask about scheduling.

Tinley Park, IL

  • 19,302 owner-occupied homes
  • 2,756 rented
  • 88% owner-occupied
  • Median value $289,000
  • Median build year 1987

Tinley Park is close to Orland Park in age and size of housing, roughly 1987 median build year and nearly nine in ten households owning. Same story on exteriors: the original builder finish is long past done and the second repaint is the one that has to be prepped properly, because the first one usually was not.

Homer Glen, IL

  • 7,480 owner-occupied homes
  • 521 rented
  • 93% owner-occupied
  • Median value $400,000
  • Median build year 1988

Homer Glen is late 1980s construction on larger lots, about 93 percent owner-occupied, with a median value around $400,000. Big exterior surface area is the whole theme: long elevations, a lot of soffit and fascia, and cedar or engineered trim now well past its first repaint. The second exterior on a house like this is the one that has to be prepped honestly, because the builder finish was carrying the job right up until it stopped.

Mokena, IL

  • 6,554 owner-occupied homes
  • 673 rented
  • 91% owner-occupied
  • Median value $377,100
  • Median build year 1996

Mokena is 1990s construction, larger homes and very high owner occupancy. That mostly means big exterior surface area and interiors with two story entries and vaulted rooms. Height is its own price tier: a two story foyer is not a room rate job, and anybody quoting it as one has not looked at it properly.

Frankfort, IL

  • 6,244 owner-occupied homes
  • 346 rented
  • 95% owner-occupied
  • Median value $461,600
  • Median build year 2000

Frankfort is the newest and highest value housing in the whole service area, median build year around 2000. Newer does not mean less work. It means large elevations, tall interior volumes and finishes that were specified once and never touched since. It is the furthest point on this list, so it is worth a conversation about travel before anybody drives out.

Lemont, IL

  • 5,524 owner-occupied homes
  • 810 rented
  • 87% owner-occupied
  • Median value $447,800
  • Median build year 1994

Lemont has the second highest median home value on this list, around $447,800, and a median build year of 1994. Newer and larger, with the problems that go with that: two story elevations, tall interior volumes, and millwork a builder specified once and nobody has touched since. A two story entry is not a room-rate job. Lemont also sits west of the rest of this list, so scheduling is a genuine conversation rather than a formality.

Housing figures on this page are from the U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, 2023 (tables B25003, B25034, B25035, B25077). They describe the places, not this business. Beverly and Mount Greenwood are Chicago community areas and the Census has no geography that matches a Chicago neighborhood, so their figures are for the ZIP code tabulation areas that cover them, 60643 and 60655, and both entries say so.

Questions

About the service area

Do you actually work in Chicago, or is that just on the website?

The city is real work, and it is mostly the south side. Bridgeview is a short run from Garfield Ridge, Clearing, Ashburn, Beverly and Mount Greenwood, and those neighborhoods are the same brick bungalow stock as the inner suburbs, so it is the same job. What will not be pretended here is coverage of the whole city. Chicago is enormous and heavily contested, and a north side call is better served by somebody on the north side. Ask, and you will be told which one you are before anyone schedules anything.

How far do you travel?

The shop is in Bridgeview and the close ring is where most of the work is. Further out is possible and it depends on the size of the job, because a long drive is worth it for a full exterior and not worth it for one small repair. Ask, and you will get a straight answer rather than a yes that turns into a scheduling problem.

Why does the age of my house keep coming up?

Because it is the single most useful thing to know before quoting. About 69 percent of Chicago's housing units were built before 1970, and the near southwest suburbs have median build years between 1947 and 1977. That means plaster as well as drywall, heavy trim, more coats of old paint, and the federal lead-safe rule for anything built before 1978. The far south and southwest towns are the opposite profile: Mokena, Frankfort, Lemont and Homer Glen are 1988 to 2000 construction, where the issue is not old paint but big elevations and tall interiors.

Do you work for landlords and property managers?

Yes, and it is an obvious fit here that nobody local seems to advertise. Blue Island is the only suburb on this list where renters outnumber owners, Justice runs just under half rental, Chicago Ridge is not far behind, and Alsip and Bridgeview are both around a third. Turnover repaints between tenants are steady, repeatable work. The van says Maintenance Service on it, and this is what that means.

Do you do commercial work?

Small local commercial, yes: offices, a retail unit, common areas in a building. Bedford Park in particular is barely residential, with fewer than 200 occupied households in the whole village, so anything there is going to be this kind of work. Large commercial contracts are a different business with different requirements and are better off with a company that only does that.
